description: Per-candidate backfill rows for #58 (track #50). Researched and run 2026-09-02. NO RECORD SECTION, exactly as the issue says: Holberg has held no public office - he was a middle-school math teacher on the West Side and then founded the financial-wellness company Spring (formerly Holberg Financial, sold to Mariner in 2023) - so there is nothing to populate a `record` array with, and no record was manufactured out of private-sector work. Positions only. The recency cutoff (2016-01-01, per the issue comment) excludes nothing: he announced 2025-10-06 and every source below is from 2026. HOW THIS WAS RUN. The issue text asks for a Workflow with Fable orchestrating and Sonnet/Opus subagents. It was run the way #56, #57 and #59 were instead - direct research plus the local CLI - because CLAUDE.md's subagent-injection note (docs/security-note-subagent-injection.md) makes a research subagent's conclusions untrusted data, and every URL below was fetched and read in this session before it became a row. Stated here so the deviation is visible rather than silent. WHAT WAS SEARCHED, AND WHAT DOES NOT EXIST. All three podcast feeds in sources.json were pulled in full and grepped: Ben Joravsky (2556 items back to 2019-02), Fran Spielman (368 items back to 2018-08) and City Cast Chicago (1383 items back to 2021-03). ZERO Holberg hits in any of them - a real null, not an unrun search. The City Club of Chicago YouTube feed likewise has no Holberg entry, and no candidate forum appearance was found anywhere. THE REAL DEAL Q&A DOES NOT EXIST FOR HIM. That questionnaire series is the best source class this track has found (#57) and it has published Brewer, Cardenas and Mendoza; as of 2026-09-02 the only Real Deal coverage naming Holberg is campaign-finance reporting (2026-06-25 and 2026-08-13). Same 'not yet published' state as lisa-nee - re-check when the remaining issues run. HIS OWN WRITING IS REAL BUT NOT ABOUT HOUSING. The #97 ruling puts candidate-authored op-eds in scope and he has three - Chicago Tribune 2026-06-05 (buy back the parking meters), Chicago Tribune 2026-07-09 (lead service lines, $150-per-home filters) and Streetsblog Chicago 2026-07-16 (a five-point CTA safety plan). None is about housing, so none is a row, by the same rule that excluded the cardenas property-tax op-ed. THE HOLBERG PLAN IS A BOOK, not a fetchable source: joeforchicago.com/the-holberg-plan is a sales page whose text is chapter blurbs plus a reserve-your-copy form ($18.71 print). The housing blurb - 'Why the affordability crisis is a supply crisis, and how we build in every neighborhood without displacing the people already there' - is a table of contents, not a position, and the book itself cannot be ingested. Noted so the next person does not re-litigate it. HIS BLUESKY FEED WAS READ IN FULL (95 posts, 2025-10-30 to 2026-08-26) and is not a row. It is where the Inc. profile and the Streetsblog op-ed surfaced, which is why it was read at all (#59: a candidate's press page is not the list of their sources), but its housing content is slogans with no instrument - 'More housing. Better use of vacant land. Stronger neighborhoods near transit', 'We have public transit. We have space. We should be building more housing right here', 'Vacant land should mean opportunity, not neglect' - and the substance behind them is in the WBEZ interview below, in his own voice, at length. WHAT ELSE WAS FETCHED AND READ IN FULL AND EXCLUDED, not skipped on assumption. CBS News Chicago (6,043 chars, read end to end): budget, CTA, ShotSpotter and 'reducing spending while lowering and freezing property taxes' - not one housing sentence, and the property-tax-only rule that excluded the cardenas op-ed applies here too. Inc. 2026-08-14 (2,633 chars): affordability as biography, no housing. The Daily Line profile: hard paywall, 1,447 fetchable chars of unrelated day-book entries. CAN TV's Chicago Newsroom 2.0 (YouTube kfNufufUsL8, 58 min, 2026-01-15) carries a Holberg segment at t=1181 but is a multi-segment roundtable with guest co-hosts and four unrelated topics - the same attribution risk that made #59 skip WTTW's full Chicago Tonight episode, so it is excluded on the same grounds. TWO ROWS USE `html_file` (#101). news.wttw.com now returns a Cloudflare interstitial and wgntv.com a PerimeterX captcha to a residential IP with a full browser UA - repeated attempts across three header profiles, all 403 - so both pages were saved from a real browser into `.playwright-mcp/` (gitignored, so the saved HTML is not committed) and passed as `html_file`. Every guard still runs against those bytes; the hosted reviewer will report both URLs `unverifiable`, which is expected and correct (#69), and `pipeline review` was therefore also run locally where the pages are readable. THE ROUNDUPS ARE DELIBERATELY NOT ROWS. Block Club's 'Who Is Running For Chicago Mayor?' (2026-08-10) and FOX 32's (2026-08-26) both report the 100,000-unit goal - 'with a goal of building 100,000 new units, at 25,000 per year, he recently said' - but as reporter paraphrase, not as anything he is quoted saying. CLAUDE.md's rule is to prefer the candidate's own answer over the reporter's summary of it, and the WBEZ row below is him saying it himself with the arithmetic attached, so the paraphrase is not needed and is not cited. Recorded here because it is the corroboration that made the WBEZ row worth transcribing. THE PRIORITIES ROW IS A DELIBERATE RE-RUN OF AN EXISTING EVIDENCE FILE, not a new one. `outlet`, `title` and `date` are set to exactly the values behind the existing id `2026-07-09-joe-holberg-for-mayor-our-vision-for-chicago`, because `make_evidence_id` is date+outlet+title: leave any of them to the page and the run writes a SECOND evidence file for the same URL, and feed.astro plus buildCandidateProfile render every evidence file, so the platform page would publish twice. Matching the identity makes the new extraction supersede the old two-statement one, which was taken from the section's intro sentences and missed the Key Ideas bullets underneath them ('rehabilitation of distressed properties', 'leverage vacant and foreclosed properties', 'faster permitting'). ROW ORDER IS WEAKEST FIRST, STRONGEST LAST, because run_backfill processes rows in file order and write_stance is last-write-wins wherever no guard applies: WGN (a diagnosis of the problem) then WTTW (one sentence) then the platform page then WBEZ, which is the only source where he names an instrument. RUN LOG 2026-09-02. All four rows ran locally from a residential IP. Raw result: 15 housing statements across 4 sources, 6 stance cells. AFTER HAND REVIEW: 9 statements across 3 sources and 4 cells, of which 3 statements and 3 cells carry a mechanism - the first non-null mechanisms this candidate has ever had. What survived and what did not is below; every deletion was made by reading the written files, which is the only thing that catches this (CLAUDE.md). THE WBEZ ROW IS THE WHOLE PR. An hour of first-person answers with a host pressing for specifics produced the three mechanisms: 'my plan is to call for 100,000 new units of housing', then - asked 'How and where would those new units be built?' - 'the city itself owns 10,000 vacant lots... getting four or six units onto each one of those lots', and the property-tax arithmetic '$3,000 average bill... you're generating $300 million in additional property taxes'. This is #52's rule holding again: an hour of answers beats any amount of announcement coverage. THE WGN EVIDENCE FILE WAS RUN AND THEN DELETED, and it is the main judgment call in this PR. It returned 4 statements and 3 of them were affirmatively wrong: (1) a budget-mismanagement quote filed as affordable-housing-funding / OPPOSES - neither the topic nor the polarity is right, and on a housing matrix 'opposes affordable housing funding' is the exact falsehood #57 exists to prevent; (2) the reporter's own sentence, 'In an interview with WGN Political Editor Tahman, Holberg says housing and affordability will be some of the top issues for his campaign', extracted as though it were his words with attribution_flag false - not a quote from him at all; (3) and (4) the SAME quote ('People's rents are going up. Their pathways to homeownership are collapsing') split across tenant-protections and affordable-housing-funding, which is the tell that the extractor was stretching. The survivor is a diagnosis of the problem, not a position: he names no instrument and proposes nothing, and labelling it `supports` asserts a position he did not state in that interview. Deleting the file rather than leaving the bad statements uncited is deliberate and follows #59, and the rendering was checked rather than assumed: feed.astro maps every evidence file's is_housing statements to a 'Featuring: <candidate>' line plus a topic tag per statement, and buildCandidateProfile puts every evidence file on the candidate's timeline; neither reads `citations`, so an uncited statement still publishes his name against 'Tenant protections' and 'Affordable housing funding'. Note the precise limit of that: neither view renders a statement's stance or summary - the profile timeline shows only date/outlet/type/title - so what an uncited bad statement leaks is the topic tag, not the 'opposes' label. That is still wrong and still public, and the statement remains in the committed record either way. TWO MORE WBEZ STATEMENTS WERE DELETED for the same reason. One filed a homelessness cell off 'in order to pursue a socially liberal agenda where we are supporting the unhoused like I was, you know, in college when I slept in my car' - the transcript context is the question 'How do you identify yourself politically?', so this is autobiography inside an answer about ideology, not a homelessness position, and it is the same shape as the lisa-nee CHA cell that #59 deleted. The other filed 'affordability comes through growth, not the other way around' under affordable-housing-funding; in the transcript that sentence sits in the property-tax passage and is a general growth philosophy, not a housing-funding position. Both were at the tail of the statement list, so removing them did not reindex any surviving citation. THE TENANT-PROTECTIONS CELL IS DELETED, and this is the loudest change in the PR. The old cell cited the platform page's intro sentence, 'Every Chicagoan deserves a safe, affordable place to call home while working to ensure residents are not displaced from their neighborhood.' The re-extraction prefers the Key Ideas bullets underneath that sentence and no longer returns it. That was MEASURED, not assumed: the priorities page was run four times (once live, three more into a scratch --data-dir) and the displacement sentence came back zero times out of four, while the four bullets came back every time. Combined with the WGN deletion, nothing anywhere in his coverage gives him a tenant-protections position - the topic is rent stabilization, eviction protections and just-cause, and he has never addressed any of them - so the honest state of that cell is empty. A reviewer who disagrees should restore it from the intro sentence rather than from anything new. A STALE-CITATION HAZARD THAT #72 DOES NOT COVER, worth recording. Re-running a source under the same evidence id supersedes citations only for the cells that run PROPOSES. The old tenant-protections cell cited '...our-vision-for-chicago#1'; after the re-run index 1 is a different statement (the rehab/vacant-properties bullet, now zoning-reform), so the citation still RESOLVED and CI would have stayed green while the cell pointed at a quote that no longer supported it. Nothing catches this but reading the file. It is moot here because the cell is deleted, but the shape - a superseded source silently re-pointing an un-reproposed cell - is a seventh way write_stance can leave a cell wrong. THE ZONING-REFORM TOPIC ASSIGNMENT IS A JUDGMENT CALL FOR THE HUMAN REVIEWER. The 4-6-units-per-lot answer is filed under zoning-reform and the summary says 'implying zoning changes'. He never says the word zoning. The local reviewer confirmed the statement and independently raised the same point, calling the implication reasonable given the density involved; the hedge is left in the summary rather than removed so the inference stays visible. REVIEW WAS RUN LOCALLY (#69) over all three surviving evidence files: 9 confirmed, 0 unverifiable, 0 contradicted, label ai-verified. Both `html_file` rows were re-fetched successfully by the reviewer's own ingest even though four curl attempts had 403'd minutes earlier - another instance of the CLAUDE.md rule that these blocks are intermittent and CI should not be written off after one 406. Expect the hosted run to differ. ONE ARTIFACT NOTE: the CLI writes a per-candidate PR body to '<slug>.md' in the repo root and .gitignore covers 'pr_body.md' but not that name, so 'joe-holberg.md' shows up as untracked after a backfill. Deleted by hand here, not committed; the gitignore gap is the #71 accident class and is worth one line, but it is a non-data change and was left out of this PR. TWO RENDERING FACTS CHECKED WHILE REVIEWING THE CELLS, both of which change how a mechanism string should be read. First, the site NEVER renders the mechanism text: index.astro and candidates/[slug].astro show only its ABSENCE (a vague dot on the matrix, 'No specific mechanism stated' on the profile), because when a mechanism exists the summary restates it and the quote sits directly below. This matters for property-taxes-tif, whose mechanism string - 'generating $300 million in additional property taxes from 100,000 new units' - reads like a tax INCREASE stripped of its summary, when his position is to freeze and lower them and the $300M is his argument for how growth pays for that. No reader sees it stripped; the field's jobs are marking the matrix, choosing which statement a cell cites, and giving review.py something checkable. Left as the extractor wrote it, flagged here. Second, ALL THREE MECHANISMS ARE ONE PLAN seen from three topics - 100,000 units, the 10,000 city lots at four-to-six units each that get you there, and the property-tax arithmetic that argues it pays for itself. Read '3 of 9 statements name an instrument' as one instrument described three times, not three instruments.
